summary: The End, the realm at the end of the old roads: a Warden and his houses, the Archive, a watch on the last shore and a north that is best not looked at too long.

endarils_watch_spirit.name: Endaril's Watch
endarils_watch_spirit.desc: A Warden who listens to everything that passes the last road misses little of what is coming.

warden_for_life.name: A Warden for Life
warden_for_life.desc: One voice holds the seat until death, and the houses have learned to follow it.

wardens_by_turns_spirit.name: Wardens by Turns
wardens_by_turns_spirit.desc: The seat passes between the houses in order, and every house has a stake in keeping the peace.

deep_orchards_spirit.name: Deep Orchards
deep_orchards_spirit.desc: Terraced orchards feed the End's many, though the labour is long and the cloth coarse.

end_provides.name: The End Provides
end_provides.desc: A remote realm that makes what it needs, and trades what it does not.

star_readers_spirit.name: The Star-Readers
star_readers_spirit.desc: The tables of the star-readers guide the steersmen, the planters and the scholars alike.

last_shore_watch.name: Watch on the Last Shore
last_shore_watch.desc: Watchers in grey towers see every sail on the cold sea.

edge_of_the_woods.name: The Edge of the Woods
edge_of_the_woods.desc: The dark is at the border, and every tree is a post and every strand a wall.

great_watch.name: The Great Watch
great_watch.desc: The End's numbers stand as a watch on every road, never as a host that marches.

the_end_holds.name: The End Holds
the_end_holds.desc: The first landing is broken and the whole realm stands behind its wardens.

the_warden_speaks.title: The Warden Speaks
the_warden_speaks.desc: Endaril rises in the grey hall and says that the houses may have only one thing in the coming year: the Archive, whose rolls are older than any crown, or the shore, whose towers are fewer than the dark hours.

merchants_whisper.title: Merchants Whisper
merchants_whisper.desc: A merchant of the quays tells the Warden that courts across the rift are gathering ships, steersmen and timber past any trade's needs. He has been offered a high price for the End's black yew, and has not yet said yes.

black_ships_seen.title: Black Ships off the Last Shore
black_ships_seen.desc: Fishers return from the northern strand with a tale of lights moving among black islands where nothing should live. They say the lights keep step with the tide, and they will not say more.

focuses.name: The Warden's Seat
focuses.desc: The Warden of the End sits where the old roads stop, in a hall of grey stone that no one remembers raising. Endaril presides over the houses, and the houses, for once, listen.

focuses.name: Endaril's Watch
focuses.desc: Endaril keeps a watch on all that passes the last road: pedlars, pilgrims and the weather. The Warden's office has always been more about listening than ruling.

focuses.name: The Houses of the End
focuses.desc: Every house of the End keeps its own hearth and its own tale. The Warden asks only that they tell the tales to each other more often than they tell them against each other.

focuses.name: The Long Memory
focuses.desc: The End remembers what other realms have let slip. Its elders recite the long rolls at the turning of the year, and the young learn them by heart.

focuses.name: A Warden for Life
focuses.desc: The Warden holds the seat until the Warden dies. The office is old and the Wardens have been few, and the houses see no reason to make it shorter.

focuses.name: Wardens by Turns
focuses.desc: The seat passes between the great houses in a fixed order, a lifetime for each. No house grows too proud, and none is quite sure it will see its turn.

focuses.name: The End Endures
focuses.desc: Whatever else comes down the old roads, the hall at their end will stand, and the houses within it will know each other by name.

focuses.name: Wellsprings of the End
focuses.desc: Cold springs well from the grey rock at the world's edge, and the houses wall them and build their first workshops beside the water.

focuses.name: Deep Orchards
focuses.desc: Orchards are planted in terraces down the sheltered valleys, and their roots go deeper than any frost. The End has never gone hungry for long.

focuses.name: Stone Roads of the End
focuses.desc: The old roads are relaid in grey stone, and the milestones, long worn smooth, are cut again with the names of the houses that tend them.

focuses.name: Essence Workshops
focuses.desc: Distillers and dyers set up beside the orchards to draw the oils and tinctures that the elves prize above gold.

focuses.name: Shipyards of the End
focuses.desc: On the last shore, where the cold sea begins, the houses raise slipways and cut keels from the dark timber of the northern slopes.

focuses.name: The End Provides
focuses.desc: What the orchards, springs and slipways make is traded along the old roads to the south, and the End finds that its remoteness has become a kind of wealth.

focuses.name: The Archive of the End
focuses.desc: In a hall older than Aenor's crown the scribes of the End copy rolls by hand, as they have always done. A fire is never lit in the room where the oldest are kept.

focuses.name: Rolls of the First Age
focuses.desc: The oldest rolls are brought down from the upper shelves and read aloud: cures, songs, boundary-lays and the names of rivers that no longer run.

focuses.name: The Star-Readers
focuses.desc: On the last shore the sky is wide and the nights are long. The star-readers set down what the heavens do, year on year, and their tables are trusted by every steersman who knows them.

focuses.name: Lore of the Unbinding
focuses.desc: The scribes copy out what the Third Age learned about lifting curses, in case the knowledge is needed again. The rolls say much about the binding, and nothing about where a wise man might be found.

focuses.name: Rolls of the First Men
focuses.desc: The archive's oldest rolls of the First Men are brought out and laid beside the tale of [zin_loc_eindil]. The seals, the names and the lines of descent agree, and the scribes put their pens down.

focuses.name: Watch the Last Shore
focuses.desc: Towers of grey stone stand along the final coast, and a watcher sits in each through the long nights, looking out over the cold sea and the narrow rift.

focuses.name: Beacon Towers
focuses.desc: Every tower is given a beacon and a stock of dry wood, and every watcher a horn. A flame at the shore reaches the Warden's hall before the sun has crossed a hand's breadth.

focuses.name: Silver Sails
focuses.desc: Pale sails are cut for the End's few ships. They are light enough to outrun weather, and bright enough that a friend can find them at dusk.

focuses.name: Quays of the End
focuses.desc: A sheltered cove below the Warden's hall is walled and quayed. Ships that come to the End now have somewhere to lie, and the End has somewhere to watch them from.

focuses.name: Merchants Whisper
focuses.desc: Merchants tell of eastern courts gathering ships, steersmen and timber in quantities no trade could need. The Warden listens to all of them, and believes more than he says.

focuses.name: Eyes on the Black North
focuses.desc: Fishers on the northern shore speak of lights among black islands where no one lives. The Warden does not dismiss them, and he does not repeat them either.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Black Shore
focuses.desc: A chain of small forts is built along the northern strand, each manned by wardens who do not discuss what they have seen out on the water.

focuses.name: The Edge of the Woods
focuses.desc: The dark has come to the edge of the woods, and the End is the last green thing before it. Every tree on the northern slope has become a post, and every post a watcher.

focuses.name: With the Kin
focuses.desc: The Warden sends gifts of dark apples and grey wool to the great groves, and asks only that the kin remember the End at the turning of the year.

focuses.name: The Kindred Called
focuses.desc: The Kindred of the Woods has been raised to defend elven land. The End takes its place without ceremony, as it has taken every duty laid on it.

focuses.name: Healers from the End
focuses.desc: The End has more herbalists than it needs, and its healers leave in twos and threes, walking down the old roads to wherever there is fever.

focuses.name: The End Keeps the Refusal
focuses.desc: Whenever men ask for hosts, the End gives them healers. The Warden restates the Refusal in a hall whose roof has sheltered it since before the Third Age.

focuses.name: Wardens of the End
focuses.desc: The wardens of the End are the most numerous in the Magical Lands and the least eager to leave home. They drill in the cold, in all weathers, and they do not boast.

focuses.name: Archers of the End
focuses.desc: Black yew from the northern slopes makes the End's longbows. They are heavy to draw and long in the shaft, and an archer takes ten years to master one.

focuses.name: White Riders
focuses.desc: White deer from the high moors are trained to carry a rider across ice and bog. They are fleet, quiet, and unafraid of the dark.

focuses.name: The Great Watch
focuses.desc: The End's numbers are gathered not as a host but as a watch: companies in rotation on every road, tower and ford. It is a host that never marches and never sleeps.

focuses.name: The End Stands
focuses.desc: The horns sound from the last shore to the Warden's hall. The End has never been conquered, and its people have no intention of being the first to learn how.

focuses.name: Hold the Last Shore
focuses.desc: Every cove, ford and strand is manned. Stone is rolled into the roads, and the wardens take their stations along the cliff-tops.

focuses.name: The Kin Ride to the End
focuses.desc: Kin from the great groves ride the long road north to stand beside the End's wardens. They have never been asked to come so far, and they come anyway.

focuses.name: Throw Them Back
focuses.desc: The first landing is broken on the grey rock, and the defenders drive it back into the surf. Whatever comes next will find the End awake.

focuses.name: The Last Shore Is Quiet
focuses.desc: The war is over and the sea is empty. The watchers climb back to their towers, and the Warden writes one line in the long rolls.
